Mission 1.30 §4. An explicit, reviewed mapping from EXACT source-native identifiers onto a canonical subject, so that Evidence from two source families can enter one Opportunity packet. Every entry names a full source-native subject key verbatim and states the basis on which a person decided the two identifiers name the same subject. There is NO string distance, NO token overlap, NO stem, NO synonym table, NO embedding and NO threshold: an identifier appears here or it does not, and an unmapped identifier keeps its source-native key and its own packet.

THIS IS NOT SAME_PROBLEM_FAMILY UNDER ANOTHER NAME. That relation asks whether two OBSERVATIONS express the same problem, is a judgement about meaning, and is PARKED (Mission 1.27). This asserts that two IDENTIFIERS, in two published vocabularies, name the same SUBJECT -- a question a person answers by reading two pages, recorded once, and checkable by anybody who reads the same two pages.

A subject_id is OURS and is not a source identifier. It is deliberately lowercase and unadorned so that nobody mistakes it for a Wikipedia article title or a Stack Overflow tag.

MISSION 1.34 (1.1.0). Every subject now declares `scope_type`: WHAT LEVEL OF THING it is, from the vocabulary PRODUCT | CATEGORY | MARKET | GEOGRAPHY. It is a property of the subject, declared by the person who wrote the entry, and the description already said it in prose. IT IS NOT A PARENT AND NOT A RELATION: nothing here says what contains `docker`, and Mission 1.34 deliberately adds no such edge -- Mission 1.33 refused to assert which commercial category contains it, and inventing one to demonstrate an architecture would be exactly the move both missions exist to refuse.
identifier_key_format: <source_id>:<scheme>:<part>|<part>...  -- the exact string SubjectKey renders, matched by equality and never by pattern

subjects.description: The Docker container platform, as a subject of published material. NOT the company, NOT a market, NOT a product this project proposes.

identifiers.basis: The English Wikipedia article whose title is `Docker_(software)`. The parenthetical disambiguator is the encyclopedia's own, and it exists precisely to separate the container platform from the other things called Docker -- so the identifier is more specific than the word, not less.

The Stack Overflow tag `docker`. Stack Overflow publishes a description for each tag and maintains tag synonyms, so the tag is a curated site identifier rather than a free-text match on a word: a question about a dock worker does not receive it. The tag is a SUBJECT and not a problem (Mission 1.18), which is exactly the granularity this registry maps.

subjects.scope_type_basis: Docker is one bounded, separately identifiable piece of software published under its own name. It is not a classification containing several things and not a space of economic exchange, so PRODUCT is the level and no other level in the vocabulary fits it.

subjects.description: The Kubernetes container orchestration system, as a subject of published material.

identifiers.basis: The English Wikipedia article titled `Kubernetes`. It needs no disambiguator because the encyclopedia records no other subject under that title.

The Stack Overflow tag `kubernetes`. Mapped for completeness of the registry; NO Evidence reaches this identifier today, because the questions this deployment holds under it arrived through a `tagged=docker` query and are a biased subset rather than a count (Mission 1.30 §0).

subjects.scope_type_basis: Kubernetes is one bounded, separately identifiable piece of software published under its own name. It is not a classification containing several things and not a space of economic exchange, so PRODUCT is the level and no other level in the vocabulary fits it.

subjects.description: The Podman container engine, as a subject of published material.

identifiers.basis: The Stack Overflow tag `podman`. Mapped for completeness; NO Evidence reaches this identifier today, because this deployment holds no questions carrying it.

subjects.scope_type_basis: Podman is one bounded, separately identifiable piece of software published under its own name. It is not a classification containing several things and not a space of economic exchange, so PRODUCT is the level and no other level in the vocabulary fits it.

deliberately_absent.container_tooling: There is no canonical subject grouping Docker, Podman and Kubernetes together. They are three subjects and stay three packets. A registry entry uniting them would be an assertion that questions and pageviews about one bear on the others -- a judgement about meaning, which is the PARKED relation reached by hand instead of by a classifier. Doing it deterministically would not make it deterministic; it would make it unargued.
deliberately_absent.docker_compose: The Stack Overflow tag `docker-compose` is NOT mapped to the `docker` subject. It is a different tool with its own tag, and folding it in would be a synonym judgement this registry has no basis for. 25 held questions carry it, which is exactly the kind of number that makes an unjustified merge tempting.
